description: An assistant superintendent for teaching and learning must approve a kindergarten reading-intervention package and its implementation plan, with input from a literacy coach, a special education coordinator, and a family liaison.

agents.name: Dr. Morgan Lee
agents.role: Assistant Superintendent for Teaching and Learning

shared_context.S1: The district is choosing a kindergarten reading-intervention package for use beginning next fall.
shared_context.S2: The two packages under review are Cedar Path and Birch Bridge.
shared_context.S3: Cedar Path scored higher than Birch Bridge in the district's instructional-rubric review and is the package named in the current draft recommendation.
shared_context.S4: Dr. Lee has final approval authority for the package and its implementation plan.
shared_context.S5: The district's adoption meeting follows a routine round-robin review in which the literacy coach, special education coordinator, and family liaison each report implementation considerations before Dr. Lee records the final plan.

PF1.text: The completed Cedar Path pilot observation showed that kindergarten intervention groups need four sessions per week, not the three sessions in the draft plan, to complete the package's core sequence; Ms. Shah finished coding the observation data after the draft was circulated and has not entered the result in the adoption file.

PF2.text: The Cedar Path student-materials review found that the adopted package must include decodable readers at levels 1 through 3; Mr. Ortiz completed the accessibility review after the draft was circulated and has not added this requirement to the materials checklist.

PF3.text: Family testing confirmed that the launch materials must be provided as take-home packets in English, Spanish, and Vietnamese rather than through an English-only online guide; Ms. Nguyen completed the family check after the draft was circulated and has not updated the outreach plan.

acceptance_conditions: Kindergarten intervention must occur four sessions per week.
Student materials must include decodable readers at levels 1 through 3.
Family guides must be available in English, Spanish, and Vietnamese.
Family guides must be distributed as take-home packets.
A formal instructional-schedule implementation commitment must be recorded.
A formal student-materials implementation commitment must be recorded.
A formal family-outreach implementation commitment must be recorded.
The family-access finding must be cited by the decision-maker after being spoken aloud.

decisive_facts.why: The pilot observation changes the intervention schedule from the draft's three sessions per week to exactly four sessions per week and requires the instructional-schedule commitment.
The accessibility review changes the student-materials decision to decodable readers at exactly levels 1 through 3 and requires the student-materials commitment.
The family check changes the guide languages to exactly English, Spanish, and Vietnamese, changes delivery to take-home packets, and requires the family-outreach commitment and citation.
